status: G5 first batch: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g5-ballista, in Chapters IV, V, IX and XII (on the web in Chapter V only)
use: Siege artillery behind the Roman line: a two-armed stone-thrower beyond the board's west edge, in the sieges. The redo of g5-ballista.

generator.prompt: A Roman two-armed torsion stone-thrower built of heavy brown weathered oak: a massive square timber frame standing upright at the front, holding two thick vertical skeins of twisted tan rope, each bound at top and bottom by a round black iron washer; two stout wooden arms swept back from the skeins and joined by a thick rope bowstring; a long timber trough running back from the frame to a wooden winch with spoked handles at the rear; the whole engine resting on a low heavy timber platform. About two and a half metres long and one point six metres high. Brown oak timber, tan rope and black iron fittings. Single isolated static prop for a grounded painterly-realistic historical game set in the third century Roman world. Physically based aged materials, believable hand-made construction and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above, restrained surface detail, level base and complete geometry from every side. No environment, ground plane, decorative display plinth, modern materials, text, logos or people.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the battles in the desktop build at High
review.notes: A brown oak torsion engine: an upright square frame holding two twisted rope skeins, its arms behind them, a trough running back to the winch, all on a low timber platform, as asked; its colour map is brown oak (no grey) and its springs are rope. Processed at 1.6 m: 1.92 by 1.25 m. Ships as g5-ballista.
